intro.quote: In this document, we enhance the existing BGP route refresh mechanisms [RFC2918] to provide for the demarcation of the beginning and the ending of a route refresh (which refers to the complete re-advertisement of the Adj-RIB-Out to a peer, subject to routing policies).

steps.explain: The route refresh is initiated in response to a normal route refresh request from the peer.

cite.quote: Before the speaker starts a route refresh that is either initiated locally, or in response to a "normal route refresh request" from the peer, the speaker MUST send a BoRR message.

steps.explain: The speaker sends a BoRR message before it starts the route refresh.

cite.quote: Before the speaker starts a route refresh that is either initiated locally, or in response to a "normal route refresh request" from the peer, the speaker MUST send a BoRR message.

steps.explain: The speaker completes the re-advertisement of the entire Adj-RIB-Out to the peer before sending the EoRR message.

cite.quote: After the speaker completes the re-advertisement of the entire Adj-RIB-Out to the peer, it MUST send an EoRR message.

steps.explain: After the re-advertisement is complete, the speaker sends an EoRR message to the peer.

cite.quote: After the speaker completes the re-advertisement of the entire Adj-RIB-Out to the peer, it MUST send an EoRR message.

intro.quote: In processing a ROUTE-REFRESH message from a peer, the BGP speaker MUST examine the "message subtype" field of the message and take the appropriate actions.

steps.explain: On receiving a BoRR message, the speaker marks all routes for the given Address Family Identifier and Subsequent Address Family Identifier from that peer as stale.

cite.quote: When a BGP speaker receives a BoRR message from a peer, it MUST mark all the routes with the given Address Family Identifier and Subsequent Address Family Identifier, <AFI, SAFI> [RFC2918], from that peer as stale.

steps.explain: The re-advertised routes replace corresponding stale routes as the receiving speaker receives them.

cite.quote: As it receives routes from its peer's subsequent Adj-RIB-Out re-advertisement, these replace any corresponding stale routes.

steps.explain: On receiving an EoRR message, the speaker immediately removes routes from the peer that remain stale for the given <AFI, SAFI>.

cite.quote: When a BGP speaker receives an EoRR message from a peer, it MUST immediately remove any routes from the peer that are still marked as stale for that <AFI, SAFI>.

intro.quote: The error handling specified in this section is applicable only when a BGP speaker has received the "Enhanced Route Refresh Capability" from a peer.

steps.explain: The BGP speaker must ignore a received ROUTE-REFRESH message whose Message Subtype is not 0, 1, or 2 and should log an error.

cite.quote: When the BGP speaker receives a ROUTE-REFRESH message with a "Message Subtype" field other than 0, 1, or 2, it MUST ignore the received ROUTE-REFRESH message.  It SHOULD log an error for further analysis.

intro.quote: The error handling specified in this section is applicable only when a BGP speaker has received the "Enhanced Route Refresh Capability" from a peer.

steps.explain: A received ROUTE-REFRESH message with Message Subtype 1 or 2 and a length other than 4 causes the BGP speaker to send a NOTIFICATION response.

cite.quote: If the length, excluding the fixed-size message header, of the received ROUTE-REFRESH message with Message Subtype 1 and 2 is not 4, then the BGP speaker MUST send a NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code of "ROUTE-REFRESH Message Error" and the subcode of "Invalid Message Length".

steps.explain: The BGP speaker sends a NOTIFICATION message with the ROUTE-REFRESH Message Error code and the Invalid Message Length subcode.
